answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post bids, then slash that stake when independent audits prove deliberate duplicate identities or fabricated work. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must acquire and immobilize capital for every persona, while risking forfeiture. For example, umber, zephyr, and vertex each need their own bond, so multiplying names does not multiply influence for free.
